correctness.rationale: Kneser's inequality forces k{0,a,b} to fill Z/cZ if the stabilizer is trivial; if it is nontrivial, the generating set reaches every vertex in the quotient in at most c/|H|-1 steps and periodicity lifts this to the same conclusion. The Apéry minimum in an equality residue is kb-1; its at-most-k-coin representative is at least kb-1, at most kb, and congruent to kb-1, forcing that exact coin value. The deficit identity then forces one copy of a, k-1 of b and b=a+1. For 2≤a<k the proposed gap is at least a(a-1) for either parity and thus is already in <a,a+1> (its quotient on division by a is at least its remainder). For odd c, the remaining a≥k give quotient k-1 and remainder a-k≤k-3; for even c, a≥k+1 gives quotient k-1 and remainder a-k-1≤k-3. The case a=1 gives equality exactly at b=2 and even c by the stated F=-1 convention. For a=k and c=2k, the candidate k²-k-1 is a gap modulo k: at least k-1 copies of k+1 would be needed and already exceed the candidate. The sharp upper bound makes that gap maximal. Independently, `python3 /workspace/branches/independent_math_replay.py 5` verified 14,665 triples through c=48 by direct integer reachability, finding 46 equalities and certifying the upper tail with c consecutive representable values per triple. This is finite corroboration only.
